title: Attention-path prefetcher and kernel winnower for mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Spike and implementation plan for a lightweight two-stage kernel selection mechanism: (1) a fast attention-path prefetcher that uses coarse-grained hardware/sequence fingerprints to pre-evaluate feasibility of kernel families, and (2) a kernel winnower that quickly eliminates candidates before running more expensive microbench probes. Goal is to reduce end-to-end tail latency for mixed prefill/decode traffic while keeping probe overhead <2% of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrated in runtime can reduce 95th percentile latency by >=6% on mixed conversational (prefill + decode) workload compared to baseline autotuner
Probe overhead measured in production-like replay traffic is <2% additional token cost
System safely falls back to existing kernel selector when probes time out or when new model ABI mismatch detected
Ship initial rollout gate and observability: per-path selection breakdown, probe success rate, and regression alerting in console
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Khan: Created ticket after spike notes — found that current autotuner probes blindly run multiple microbench kernels during warmstart, causing up to 15ms tail for short-decoding requests.

2026-03-02 Miguel Ortega: Completed first prototype of fingerprint extractor (gpu occupancy + seqlen histogram + model opset signature) paired with a tiny decision tree. Local microbench: eliminated ~40% of slow-path candidates with <0.8ms overhead.
2026-03-05 Engineering review (Ravi Patel): Requested clearer failure modes and TTL for fingerprints; suggested adding model-version hashing to avoid stale profiles after small operator changes.
2026-03-07 PM feedback (Priya Nair): Prioritize conservative thresholds for canary rollouts — emphasize no regression for P0 customers. Added release gating and observability requirements.
2026-03-10 Data from replay tests: Mixed workload (50% prefill, 50% decode) on rtx-a6000 cluster shows 95p latency -7.1% and median -2.2%; probe CPU overhead ~0.6% and token-cost delta ~1.1%.

2026-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Found instability with quantized kernel timings on certain GPU driver combos; added 'driver-stability' label in selector to force conservative probes or immediate fallback for those drivers. Creating follow-up task to expand microbench matrix.
